title: The Beginner's Guide to Neural Networks
partialText: This beginner-friendly guide explains the core mechanics of neural networks, focusing on weights, biases, gradient descent, and batch processing. Through analogies, simple Python examples, and practical learning advice, it aims to help new AI learners build an intuitive understanding of how neural networks learn and why foundational mathematics is essential.

title: Building User-Aware AI Agents with MCP and Serverless
partialText: Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets AI discover and use new tools on the fly. Each MCP server becomes a domain-specific intelligence hub that can serve multiple agents while maintaining its own security and business logic.

title: How Your Agents Produce Code Is More Valuable Than the Code Itself
partialText: When you work with agents, the data from your interactions becomes the prime commodity — the raw material for building the next iteration and training the next generation of agents to do the job more accurately and more efficiently. Even the mistakes and errors are valuable learning opportunities. It is no coincidence that the flagship coding agents came from the two leading model labs, and those same labs shipped the most advanced models right after. Your interaction with your agents is unique. It is your fingerprint, your mold — your primary IP. And to own it means holding full control over both its interface and its infrastructure.

title: Most AI Agents Aren't Really Agents At All
partialText: Drawing on the Critique of Agent Model paper, this article argues that many modern AI agents are better described as agentic workflows than genuinely agentive systems. It explores the distinction through concepts like persistent goals, adaptive identity, self-regulation, world models, and continuous learning, offering a more rigorous framework for evaluating autonomous AI.

title: The $51 Billion RWA Market Is a Mirage; Here’s Why Institutional Capital Still Won’t Flow
partialText: The RWA market may have surpassed **$50 billion** in tokenized assets, but that doesn't mean institutional capital has arrived. Tokenization solved asset representation, not capital deployment. Institutions still face fragmented wallet access, shallow liquidity, limited yield opportunities, and settlement risks that make large-scale allocation unattractive. The next phase of RWA growth depends less on creating more tokenized assets and more on building the infrastructure that lets capital move efficiently. Until distribution, liquidity, native stablecoin settlement, and institutional-grade access improve, the industry's trillion-dollar ambitions will remain more narrative than reality.

title: Convert PDF to Image in C#: The One-Liner That Isn't in 2026
partialText: Rendering PDFs to images in C# is easy. Choosing the right library for scale, fidelity, licensing, and deployment is harder.

title: How Europe Regulated Its Way Out of the Stablecoin Market
partialText: Euro stablecoins hold less than 0.3% of the dollar stablecoin market and are losing ground to the Turkish lira. MiCA was designed to bring clarity to crypto in Europe. It achieved that — and simultaneously made euro stablecoin issuance economically unviable.

title: How We Built a Global Low-Latency App Without a Traditional Backend
partialText: This article explains how to architect a globally distributed, read-heavy web application using region-local SQLite shards, SvelteKit, Bun, Fly.io, and Litestream. It explores practical design decisions that reduce latency, simplify infrastructure, and keep operating costs low without relying on a traditional backend.

title: Building a Self-Healing RAG Pipeline With LangGraph, LangChain, and LLM-as-Judge
partialText: RAG systems can confidently generate answers that contradict their own retrieved context, with no errors anywhere to flag it. This article builds a self-healing layer that validates retrieval quality before generation, verifies grounding after generation using a separate LLM-as-judge, retries once with a rewritten query on failure, and falls back to an honest "couldn't verify this" response otherwise. Every failure gets logged asynchronously to Kafka, where independent consumers automatically grow the evaluation dataset, queue documents for re-indexing, and alert on failure spikes, turning the system from one that just recovers into one that measurably improves over time. Full LangGraph implementation included.

title: What If the Fermi Paradox Is Asking the Wrong Question?
partialText: Claiming aliens don't exist just because we haven't met them is like a goldfish in a bowl claiming oceans don't exist. The silence of the universe isn't absolute proof we are alone, but could instead be a deliberate protective barrier of cosmic isolation and mismatched timelines. Ultimately, our technology might just be an accident of human biology, meaning other civilizations may have evolved in ways that are completely unfathomable to us.

title: Safety-Critical Industries Offer a Blueprint for Enterprise AI Governance
partialText: Enterprise AI in regulated industries should borrow proven safety practices from aviation and nuclear engineering rather than relying on new governance frameworks. Explainability, rigorous configuration management, continuous monitoring, human oversight, and least-privilege architectures provide a more trustworthy foundation for deploying AI in safety-critical environments.

title: Google Delays Gemini 3.5 Pro to July 17: The Strategic Play Behind the Scrapped Base Model
partialText: Google DeepMind postponed Gemini 3.5 Pro to July 17, 2026 after abandoning its original foundation in favor of a longer pre-training cycle. The move reflects growing pressure from GPT-5.6 and Claude Fable 5, as frontier AI competition shifts from incremental upgrades to major architectural leaps. While Gemini 3.5 Flash remains available, enterprise teams may need multi-model deployment strategies until Pro arrives.

title: Prediction Markets Are Entering Their Infrastructure Era
partialText:
Prediction markets hit a record $45 billion in June, driven largely by World Cup demand. But the surge exposed the harder challenge ahead: turning headline volume into deep, reliable liquidity that institutions can actually trade.

At the same time, platforms are competing to own different parts of the stack; from distribution and user access to exchange infrastructure and data, while regulatory pressure, marketing scrutiny and security failures show the sector’s systems are still catching up with its growth.

title: How Float Runs an AI Energy Company on a 3-Person Team with Tiger Data
partialText: Float built an AI platform that disaggregates 1Hz smart meter data into appliance-level energy insights. After evaluating major time-series databases, the startup chose Tiger Data, achieving 99.3% compression—well above the 90% needed to make its subscription model viable. Continuous aggregates power real-time billing, while the managed platform lets a three-person team scale efficiently.

title: Bittensor Cleans House: Inactive Subnets To No Longer Get Weekly Emissions Says Const
partialText: Bittensor is now pausing emissions weekly (every Monday) to subnets with no miner activity or missing code, per an announcement from co-founder Const. Over 50 subnets were affected in this round, though removal isn’t permanent — subnets can be reinstated case-by-case once issues are fixed. The move aligns with Bittensor’s Taoflow emission model, which rewards subnets showing real staking activity and redirects resources away from inactive ones.

title: RAG Was Read-Only. Meet the File Agent.
partialText: RAG and "chat with your docs" tools only read. A file agent acts - organizing, renaming, sharing, and signing files in plain English — and the real engineering is making it safe to act on messy files, not making it smart.

title: Fleet Safety Camera System Engineering Knowledge Series
partialText: This series comprises six main articles covering, in sequence, IQ Lab build-up, Intrinsic/Extrinsic Calibration, component selection, factory EOL testing and Active Alignment, environmental reliability testing, and customer telemetry with closed-loop optimization. The articles form a clear causal chain, starting from precise lab measurements, running through mass production validation, and ultimately returning to continuous improvement driven by field data.

title: The Smartphone Is the New Office, But Workplace Software Has Not Caught Up
partialText: Mobile work is now routine, but many workplace apps still treat phones as a backup to desktop workflows instead of a real place where work happens.
